posts.text:
Our casework team recently helped a constituent get a long-overdue tax credit for installing solar panels.

That’s one of more than 5,000 cases we’ve solved. If you need help with a federal agency, we’re here to help. https://t.co/Yzks63yd4E

Yesterday’s nationwide grounding of flights is a crisis. It stranded tens of thousands of people and raised serious questions about the safety of air travel.

This is one of those moments where reliable political leadership will make all the difference.

We need serious leaders that we trust to come clean about what happened and how to fix it. The only way to do that is if the Administration works with a bipartisan group of lawmakers - today.

This should not be a complicated or time consuming process.

Get the leading Democrats and Republicans on the leading committees - transportation, intelligence, homeland security, appropriations - into a room with Duffy, Mullin, and others.

Give them the assignment of getting to the bottom of what happened, quickly, and how to solve it, quickly. Then announce it all together.

This should take a few days.

Otherwise, we’re going to have folks blaming one another, unanswered questions about competency and corruption, and no workable solution - certainly not one most folks can trust.

They’re all over the place.

People just want to fly safely, guys. Lock in. https://t.co/XARC9RbcAE
Congratulations to Kelly Crabtree, a swimmer from Mason, on her Silver medal at the Special Olympics USA Games this year. 👏🏼👏🏼 https://t.co/AISdQQ6jVQ
Why I love school visits 👇🏻 https://t.co/CPFwQPj1sn

Democrats need to hit the ground running.

What we should focus on in the next Congress.👇🏻 https://t.co/sZPT0jGMWm

We pushed for this transparency and oversight with our “Saving Seniors Money on Prescription Drugs Act” back in February.

Excited to see our bill’s language is now being used at the Department of Labor to help lower healthcare costs for hardworking Americans. https://t.co/ABwmDZ7Y94

Government employees should never be silenced from exposing waste, fraud, abuse, and corruption.

Our bill with @CongressmanRaja would stop taxpayer dollars from being used to mandate NDAs that violate whistleblower protections. https://t.co/fkDvg1pfVx

Congress must pass the Major Richard Star Act.

It’s long past time to get our veterans the full benefits they deserve.

If it passes, combat-injured veterans will receive both their full military retirement pay and VA disability benefits.

That means an average of $1,200 more a month for veterans who have already sacrificed so much for us.
After years of waiting, the House is finally voting on the Major Richard Star Act this week.
A few Republicans finally joined us, and in September, we reached the 218 signatures needed to force a vote.

Even with a ton of support, the bill has never been voted on.

In May, @RepMarkTakano decided to file a discharge petition to force a vote on the House floor.

To succeed, a discharge petition needs 218 signatures from House members.

In the last three congresses, the bill had more than 300 cosponsors in the House.

In this Congress, it has 342 cosponsors in the House and 80 in the Senate.

Right now, more than 59,000 veterans who were injured in combat and forced to retire early aren’t getting their full military retirement pay because they also receive VA disability benefits.

This needs to change.
The Major Richard Star Act has been introduced in each of the last four Congresses.

Congress can restore thousands in earned benefits to more than 50,000 veterans this week.

Here’s how we get it done. 👇🏼🧵

What's the biggest group inside the new Democratic House majority?

The answer will surprise you. https://t.co/JQT84FVW9D

Excited to have been elected Vice Chair of the @NewDemCoalition.

We’re going to lead this fight for common-sense solutions that lower costs, make healthcare more affordable, and end corruption in Washington. 👏🏼👏🏼 https://t.co/wjOAzTDHSU
The 10 bills Congress should pass. https://t.co/4qPV6JyInJ

Today we honor the brave men and women who have served our country.

Happy Veterans Day, SW Ohio. Thank you. 🙏🏻💙 https://t.co/INls6bPL99
🙏🏼💙 https://t.co/5tlu8tVBMr
Three reasons why Pete Hegseth still needs to go 👇🏻 https://t.co/tesHnP9Bcb

In what context is it okay to treat a child this way?

It’s outrageous.

DHS should resolve this immediately. Get this kid home to his family. https://t.co/RI1OujanSm

Americans have made it clear they want change, and now it’s time for Congress to get it done.

From the economy and the tax code to housing and healthcare, we have to fix a system that is rigged against hardworking families.

Our plan to return wealth and power to the American https://t.co/2tWpWAcJ83

When the super-wealthy pay less, working families end up paying more.

How “trickle-down taxes” work 👇🏼 https://t.co/kz5fKqbINf

When Congressional Republicans give the super-wealthy tax breaks, your taxes go up.

This wouldn’t happen if the super-wealthy paid their fair share. https://t.co/JT9NZx3Plx
How my work as a teacher still guides me in Congress today👇🏼 https://t.co/SO3sbP6O18
@BAPS_PubAffairs
Our government should help hardworking Americans, not those at the top.

Billionaires and big corporations need to pay their fair share, so we can invest in housing, schools, public safety, and senior services.

When the super wealthy start paying all their taxes, your taxes get lower.
We fix this by changing the tax code in Washington.

That's how tax cuts for billionaires in Washington and at the statehouse trickle down to you, which results in higher taxes.

That’s why there are so many local levies on the ballot in Ohio.

When federal and state funding dries up, local governments have to find the money somewhere.

So they turn to you.

But here's the catch: Local governments can't just pass this on.

Our communities still need police officers, firefighters, roads, schools, and essential services.

So states start cutting funding to local governments.

That means less money for our cities, townships, schools, and the services families rely on every day.

Those federal cuts mean less funding for states.

And what do states like Ohio do? They turn around and give even more tax breaks to the wealthy and big corporations.

Now there's even less money to invest in our communities.

It starts in Washington.

Congress spends trillions on tax breaks for the super wealthy and big corporations.

Then, to help pay for those giveaways, they cut investments in housing, healthcare, education, and other essential services.

You've heard of trickle-down economics: Massive tax breaks for billionaires and big corporations and supposedly the benefits will trickle down to everyone else.

But here's what's actually trickling down: Higher taxes for working families. https://t.co/ocRc27RJpY

When Washington cuts taxes for the super wealthy, you get the bill.

How trickle-down economics leads to higher taxes for you – and why we need to change the tax code. 🧵👇🏼
